title: Solar System Orbits
description: Watch Mercury, Venus, Earth, and Mars orbit the Sun, then compare which lap takes more days.
learningObjectives: Explain why a planet farther from the Sun takes longer to complete a lap

params.description: Which planets to include when a child compares orbits.

events.name: planet_selected
events.description: The child chose a planet to look at.

events.name: orbit_comparison_completed
events.description: The child compared a closer planet with a farther one.

tutorGuide.intro: The planets are moving around the Sun. Closer ones finish a lap sooner.
steps: Read which planet is farther and how many days its lap takes.
Tap another planet and compare the two laps.
observationPrompts: Which planet is closer to the Sun, Earth or Mars?

misconceptions.belief: Every planet takes one year to go around the Sun.
misconceptions.response: A year is Earth's lap. A farther planet has a longer path, so its lap takes more days.

hints: The sentence names the closer planet and the farther one.
Farther from the Sun means a longer lap.

successCriteria.description: Compared a closer planet with a farther one

accessibility.screenReaderSummary: Four planets orbit the Sun. Tap a planet to compare its lap with a neighbor. Closer planets finish sooner.
